title: Domestication of African rice
summary: Genetic work indicates the wild grass Oryza barthii was domesticated into African rice, Oryza glaberrima, about 3,000 years ago. A 2018 genomic study inferred the cradle of this domestication to be the Inner Niger Delta in Mali. The earliest documented archaeological evidence of the crop comes from Jenne-Jeno, about 2,000 years ago.

uncertainty.note: Source says "about 3,000 years ago"; converted to a year without further precision.

importance.justification: Independent domestication of a staple cereal in West Africa.
